## Network access is unavailable — I could not complete the task

I explicitly could not reach the Wikipedia/MediaWiki API from this session. Every network-capable tool call was refused by the environment with `permission required but no prompt available`:

- `webfetch` on the exact API URL from the task (`action=query&prop=revisions&titles=Lego&rvstart=2022-12-31T23:59:59Z&rvdir=older`) — blocked, retried with URL-encoded `rvprop` — blocked
- `webfetch` on unrelated control URLs (`https://example.com/`, `rest.php/v1/page/Lego/last-edit`, `Special:Export/Lego`) — blocked, confirming this is a blanket network/tool permission issue, not a Wikipedia-side one
- `websearch` — blocked
- `screenshot` (to drive a browser locally) — blocked
- There is no shell/bash tool in this environment, so `curl` was not an option either

I also checked the project (`glob **/*.json|txt|html|wikitext`, `read package.json`) — it is empty, so there was no cached copy of the revision to fall back on.

**Therefore I have no oldid, no timestamp, and no image list to report, and I will not guess them** — any numbers I produced here would be fabricated.

## What to run instead (two steps)

1. Get the last 2022 revision's `oldid` + timestamp:
```
curl -s "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&titles=Lego&rvlimit=5&rvprop=ids%7Ctimestamp&rvstart=2022-12-31T23:59%5BT%5D23:59:59Z&rvdir=older&format=json"
```
(take `revisions[0].revid` from the response — `rvdir=older` starting at 2022-12-31T23:59:59Z gives the last edit of 2022; the follow-up `rvcontinue`/limit of 5 lets you sanity-check the timestamps are all ≤ 2022)

2. Fetch that revision's wikitext and count image embeds:
```
curl -s "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&revids=<OLDID>&rvprop=content&rvslots=main&format=json" \
 | grep -oiE '\[\[ *(File|Image):[^]|]*' | sed 's/.*[[:space:]]//' | sort -fu
```
Use `... | sort -fu | wc -l` for a de-duplicated count.

**Counting caveats to decide before trusting a raw number:** use `-u`/`sort -u` since one file can be embedded twice; include both `File:` and `Image:` prefixes plus the `[[Media:` form; decide whether `<gallery>` entries (not `[[File:` prefixed, need a separate grep), `deadlink`/`Icon` helper templates, and hidden categories count; and note external links (`http://…png`) vs. actual embeds.

If you can grant `webfetch` permission (or a shell tool), I'll rerun this and report the oldid, timestamp, the filename list, and the total.
